messages:
Tom H: quick ping — ACME deal asked for how we size queue depth vs reserved GPUs for their commit. They expect spiky bursts (5–10x) for 30m windows. can we outline guidance and a short config they can hand to infra?
Elaine S: short answer: size reserved GPUs for sustained baseline RPS + prewarm for expected spike. queue depth should be tuned to keep latency p95 under their SLO.
Sanjay R: can you share their expected token / request profile? are these short chat messages (~60 tokens) or long generations? that changes batching and GPU inject.
Tom H: they sent this: "avg 120 tokens, 90 reqs/min normally, spikes to ~900 reqs/min for 20–40m, 90% are single-turn, 10% multi-turn with 1.5x tokens". also require <300ms p95 for “fast” endpoints, <1s allowed for async batch.
Mia P: ok rough calc: baseline 90 rps? you mean 90 reqs/min -> 1.5 rps baseline. spike 900/min -> 15 rps. baseline throughput tiny. a single A10/RTX-class instance can do ~20 rps for 120-token gpt-like model depending on quant. so baseline could be 1 reserved GPU, but need headroom for 15 rps spikes + safety.
Ryan L: agree. recommend reserved_pool = 2 GPUs for commit runway, with autoscale policy to add 2 more on sustained >10 rps for 5m, and a burst pool (spot) for ephemeral up to +4. fallback to quantized variant if load > 75% and cost controls hit.
Tom H: can you sketch an autoscale policy snippet I can paste in the SOW/security doc?
Sanjay R: paste below (example):
```
# autoscale policy (pseudo)
min_replicas: 2
max_replicas: 6
scale_up_trigger:
  - type: rps
    threshold: 10    # rps per model endpoint across pool
    duration: 300s   # sustained 5m
scale_down_trigger:
  - type: rps
    threshold: 3
    duration: 600s
burst_pool: spot
burst_max: 4
fallback_model: model-x-quantized
kv_cache_warm: true
prewarm_seconds: 120
```
Mia P: note: prewarm_seconds 120 is usually enough to warm KV cache for common prefixes; for ACME we can define a preheat list from their top 50 prompts — reduces first-token latency significantly.
Tom H: security and pricing team also asked: if we recommend 2 reserved GPUs as baseline, what’s monthly cost estimate vs commit credits? Finance Bot: estimated list: reserved A10-equivalent: $6,500/mo each -> 2 = $13k/mo. burst spot usage cost variable; suggest commit discount applied -> net approx $9.1k/mo after 30% commit discount (very rough). include caveat re: longer context or larger models.
Elaine S: also add operational guardrail: queue depth cap at 200 requests queued per endpoint; beyond that, reject with 429 and redirect to degraded smaller-model route. avoids OOM and unbounded latency.
Ryan L: on billing side, call out that autoscale adds ephemeral credits billed separately; include estimated token cost for spike windows (15 rps * 120 tokens * 60s * 30m per spike) – I gave them a CSV calc in the SOW.
Tom H: perfect. final ask from ACME: security questionnaire wants network/region fallback and on-prem possibility. can we call out VPC option + AZ fallback in one paragraph?
Sanjay R: short paragraph to paste: "We support VPC Private Deployment for regulated workloads; dedicated capacity can be pinned to specific regions/AZs. In the event of AZ degradation we failover to warm regional pools with automatic routing policies. For highest assurance we recommend a 1-AZ active + 1-AZ warm standby architecture and cross-AZ KV cache warmers. Logs and KMS integrations are available for auditability."
Tom H: awesome. I'll bundle these into the SOW and send to ACME. thanks all :rocket:
